memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Israel said to Joseph, 'I am about to die, but God will be with you and take you back to the land of your fathers.'" — Gen 48:21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob says the hardest thing plainly: "I am about to die." No pretending, no softening it. And in the same breath he says the most comforting thing: "but God will be with you."

That little word "but" carries the whole weight of the verse. I am going, but God is not.

This is what every believer eventually has to hand on. We cannot stay with the people we love. Parents die, mentors move away, the people who held us up are eventually not there. What we can leave behind is the assurance that God remains.

Jacob is dying in Egypt, and he still speaks of God taking his family back to the land of their fathers. He will not see it. He believes it anyway.

Jesus said something similar to His disciples before He left them, though His was a promise no dying man could make: "Surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age" (Matt 28:20). Jacob could only point to God's presence. Christ *is* God's presence with us, and He does not die again.

Whoever leaves your life, He does not.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who have you lost that you still miss?
2. Have you learned to lean on God's presence rather than on people He gave you?
3. What assurance do you want to leave behind for those who come after you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, people I depend on will not always be here, but You will. Teach me to rest in Your presence, and let me leave behind an assurance of Your faithfulness. Amen.
